confidence_thresholds.note: These are reference defaults. Your compliance policy governs actual values.

flags.description: The counterparty's legal name matches or partially matches an entity on a sanctions watchlist. This flag is generated by name-string comparison and is subject to false positives from similarly named entities, parent companies, and transliteration variants.
regulatory_basis: OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list — 31 CFR Part 597
International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA), 50 U.S.C. §§ 1701–1706
investigation_checklist: Query OFAC SDN list by counterparty LEI (not by name) — LEI is the authoritative identifier
Query OFAC Consolidated list by counterparty LEI
Check GLEIF record for parent entity — name match may originate from a parent entity
Review KYC record for risk tier and prior flags
Review 24-month transaction history for unusual patterns
false_positive_indicators: LEI-based OFAC query returns no match
Name match is attributable to a parent entity with a similar name in a different jurisdiction
Counterparty has an active ISSUED LEI with ACTIVE entity status
KYC record is CURRENT with LOW or MEDIUM risk tier
genuine_concern_indicators: LEI-based OFAC query returns an EXACT or ALIAS match
Parent entity LEI is on the OFAC SDN list
Counterparty KYC risk tier is HIGH or PROHIBITED
Name match confidence score above 0.85 combined with a parent entity in a high-risk jurisdiction
flags.sar_consideration: File SAR if genuine concern confirmed and trade value is material. Consult your BSA Officer for the materiality threshold applicable to your institution.
flags.triage_guidance: Characterize whether the flag is likely a name-string false positive or a genuine identity match. Direct investigation agent to run LEI-based OFAC query first.

flags.description: The counterparty's Legal Entity Identifier directly matches a sanctioned entity on the OFAC SDN or Consolidated list. This is a high-confidence flag with a low false-positive rate. Immediate escalation is typically warranted.
regulatory_basis: OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list — 31 CFR Part 597
Blocking regulations applicable to the identified sanctions program
investigation_checklist: Confirm LEI match against current OFAC SDN list — verify list timestamp is within 24 hours
Identify the sanctions program associated with the matched entity (e.g. IRAN, RUSSIA, SDGT)
Check whether the trade has already been executed or is pending settlement
Review KYC record and escalate immediately if not already done
false_positive_indicators: LEI was re-issued or transferred — registration_status is TRANSFERRED or DUPLICATE
Confirmed data entry error in upstream screening system
genuine_concern_indicators: LEI query returns EXACT match with confidence_score = 1.0
Matched entity has ACTIVE entity status
Sanctions program is current and not expired
flags.sar_consideration: SAR filing is very likely required. Consult BSA Officer and legal counsel immediately. Do not disclose SAR existence to the counterparty (BSA confidentiality requirements, 31 U.S.C. § 5318(g)(2)).
flags.triage_guidance: Assign HIGH risk immediately. Direct investigation agent to confirm the LEI match and identify the sanctions program. Do not auto-clear at any confidence level.

flags.description: A single trade's value is anomalous relative to the counterparty's established 24-month trading history. Typically identified by z-score analysis against historical average trade size.
regulatory_basis: Bank Secrecy Act (BSA), 31 U.S.C. § 5318(g) — SAR filing obligation
FinCEN regulations, 31 CFR § 1023.320 — SAR requirements for broker-dealers
FINRA Rule 3310 — AML compliance program requirements
investigation_checklist: Compare current trade value against counterparty's 24-month average trade value
Check whether this is a new counterparty with no baseline (new counterparty ≠ suspicious)
Review for other concurrent AML flags on the same counterparty
Review KYC record for any business purpose statements that explain the volume change
false_positive_indicators: New counterparty relationship — no 24-month baseline available
Counterparty recently underwent a documented business change (e.g. fund size increase)
Volume spike is consistent with a known market event (e.g. index rebalancing)
genuine_concern_indicators: Trade value is more than 5x the counterparty's 24-month average
Unusual volume concurrent with other AML flags on the same counterparty
No documented business reason for volume change in KYC record
flags.sar_consideration: SAR filing warranted if unusual volume is combined with other indicators and no plausible business explanation exists.
flags.triage_guidance: Assign MED risk unless combined with another flag type. Direct investigation agent to compare against TX history baseline.

flags.description: A pattern of trades appears designed to evade BSA Currency Transaction Report (CTR) or equivalent threshold requirements. In equities, structuring manifests as a series of trades that individually fall below reporting thresholds but collectively represent a significantly larger position.
regulatory_basis: Structuring is a federal crime regardless of the legality of the underlying funds
investigation_checklist: Review 24-month transaction history for the pattern of trades that triggered this flag
Calculate the aggregate value of the suspected structuring pattern
Check whether the pattern spans multiple trading desks or accounts
Review KYC record for any explanation of the trading pattern
false_positive_indicators: Trade pattern is consistent with a documented investment strategy (e.g. algorithmic execution of a large order)
Counterparty is a market maker with known high-frequency trading patterns
Pattern resolves when controlling for market hours and liquidity constraints
genuine_concern_indicators: Trades are consistently below a single threshold value with no execution rationale
Pattern is concentrated in a short time window
Counterparty's KYC does not document a trading strategy consistent with the observed pattern
flags.sar_consideration: SAR filing is very likely required if structuring is confirmed. Structuring is itself a criminal offense under 31 U.S.C. § 5324.
flags.triage_guidance: Assign HIGH risk. Direct investigation agent to pull the full 24-month transaction pattern and calculate the aggregate value.

flags.description: A pattern of rapid buy/sell transactions with the same or related counterparty, potentially designed to obscure the origin of funds. In equities, layering often involves placing and quickly canceling or reversing trades to create a misleading appearance of market activity.
regulatory_basis: Securities Exchange Act Section 9(a)(2) — prohibition on market manipulation
investigation_checklist: Review 24-month transaction history for rapid reversal patterns with this counterparty
Check whether the counterparty appears on both sides of trades in short time windows
Calculate the net economic position after accounting for the layering pattern
Check for related counterparties (same parent entity, same beneficial owners) in the pattern
false_positive_indicators: Counterparty is a documented market maker — rapid reversals are expected
Pattern is consistent with documented hedging or arbitrage activity in KYC
Net economic position is consistent with a legitimate investment thesis
genuine_concern_indicators: Net economic position across the pattern is near-zero (no apparent investment purpose)
Pattern involves multiple related counterparties (same beneficial owners)
Concurrent with UNUSUAL_VOLUME or other AML flags
flags.sar_consideration: SAR filing warranted if layering pattern is confirmed with no legitimate business explanation.
flags.triage_guidance: Assign HIGH risk. Direct investigation agent to calculate net economic position across the pattern.

flags.description: The counterparty is domiciled in a jurisdiction identified by FATF as high-risk, non-cooperative, or under increased monitoring. Jurisdiction risk alone is not determinative — it raises the threshold for other due diligence.
regulatory_basis: FATF Recommendations — High-Risk and Other Monitored Jurisdictions
FinCEN Geographic Targeting Orders (GTOs) where applicable
investigation_checklist: Confirm counterparty's domicile jurisdiction against current FATF high-risk list
Review KYC record — high-risk jurisdiction counterparties should have ENHANCED due diligence
Check whether the jurisdiction has been subject to a FinCEN Geographic Targeting Order
Review transaction history for patterns consistent with jurisdiction-based layering
false_positive_indicators: Jurisdiction classification has changed since KYC record was last updated (FATF lists are updated quarterly)
Counterparty is a well-documented institutional entity with a long relationship history and CURRENT KYC
Counterparty's registered domicile differs from its operational headquarters
genuine_concern_indicators: Counterparty is in a currently active FATF blacklist jurisdiction
KYC record does not reflect ENHANCED status despite high-risk jurisdiction flag
Trade pattern is inconsistent with stated business purpose in KYC
flags.sar_consideration: SAR filing warranted if jurisdiction risk is combined with other AML indicators. Jurisdiction risk alone is generally insufficient for SAR filing.
flags.triage_guidance: Assign MED risk as a baseline. Upgrade to HIGH if concurrent with other flag types or if KYC is STALE or absent.

sar_filing.title: SAR Filing Requirements (US)
sar_filing.confidentiality_requirement: SAR existence must not be disclosed to the subject of the SAR (31 U.S.C. § 5318(g)(2)). This prohibition applies to all staff.
sar_filing.note: Thresholds and deadlines are reference values. Your BSA Officer and legal counsel determine whether and when to file in specific cases. This system initiates the SAR assessment process — it does not file SARs autonomously.

kyc_review_cycles.title: KYC Review Cycle Thresholds
kyc_review_cycles.regulatory_basis: BSA, 31 U.S.C. § 5318(l); FinCEN Customer Due Diligence (CDD) Rule, 31 CFR § 1020.210

LOW.note: Standard review cycle for low-risk counterparties

MEDIUM.note: Same as low-risk unless elevated by a specific trigger

HIGH.note: Enhanced review cycle for high-risk counterparties

kyc_review_cycles.note: These are reference defaults based on FinCEN CDD Rule guidance. Your institution's AML compliance program defines the actual thresholds.

ofac_compliance.title: OFAC Sanctions Compliance
ofac_compliance.regulatory_basis: IEEPA, 50 U.S.C. §§ 1701-1706; OFAC regulations, 31 CFR Parts 500-598
ofac_compliance.query_method: Always query by Legal Entity Identifier (LEI). Name-string queries are supplementary only.
ofac_compliance.blocked_transaction_requirements: Blocked transactions must be reported to OFAC within 10 business days. Consult legal counsel immediately for any confirmed OFAC match.
